clue.text: Capital return on project initially expected to be big, clearly

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the reversed capital after the word for project

parts.note: to project is to stick out, protrude

indicators.note: return tells us to read the capital city's name backwards

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word expected

explanation.surface: An investor hopes a project will deliver a big return on capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns LIMA into AMIL; 'initially' takes E from 'expected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sticks out a mile is so conspicuous that nobody could miss it.

clue.text: Period on North and South, say, with helpful suggestions from author

parts.note: a stage is a period or phase of development
north and south are examples of compass directions

explanation.surface: A novel set in north and south comes with an author's tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North and South' looks like the Gaskell novel, but it just gives examples of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright's stage directions are the instructions in the script telling actors how to move and speak.

clue.text: Stress for poet, cold in badly-made suit

indicators.note: in puts the letter for cold inside the jumbled letters
badly-made says the letters of suit are put together wrongly

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A poet feels the stress of wearing a cheap suit in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly-made' rearranges SUIT to ITUS, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the rhythmical accent or beat falling on a syllable of verse.

clue.text: Double sink adjusted to accommodate end of pipe in twisted state

indicators.note: to accommodate means the shuffled letters take another letter inside them
adjusted signals the doubled letters are rearranged
Double means the word sink is written out twice
end of picks the closing letter of pipe

explanation.surface: A plumber fits a double sink with a twisted waste pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' gives SINKSINK, 'adjusted' rearranges it, and 'to accommodate' takes in E from 'end of pipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkiness is the condition of having many kinks or twists, as a tangled hose does.

clue.text: Facing magistrate, drunk is tense

parts.note: to be up before the magistrate is to be in court facing a charge
tight is a colloquial word for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk appearing before the magistrate is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for anxious or nervous, a synonym of tense.

clue.text: A' losing finalist, depressed and perspiring

parts.note: the letter A, the apostrophe being a stray mark in the printed text

indicators.note: finalist points to the closing letter of the word losing

parts.note: low means depressed, in low spirits

explanation.surface: A losing finalist is downcast and sweating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalist' gives G, the last letter of 'losing'; the apostrophe after A is a printing stray.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flushed and glowing from exertion is aglow, a hot, sweaty condition.

clue.text: Made cross, engraved perhaps, for bishop's induction

indicators.note: induction means bringing something in, here the bishop's letter is put inside

parts.note: read as en-graved, put in a grave, that is buried
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about a bishop's ceremony of installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engraved perhaps' plays on en-graved, placed in a grave; the 'perhaps' flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals interbred are crossed with each other to produce hybrid offspring.

clue.text: Encourage joining club with family for unserious competition

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
and is the word that joins things together
a spoon was an old lofted wooden golf club
race in the sense of lineage or family stock

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to join a club as a family member for a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOON is an old name for a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-and-spoon race is a comic school sports-day event, a contest nobody takes seriously.

clue.text: Be blown backwards, to west

indicators.note: to says the word for backwards is added to the compass letter

parts.note: aft means towards the stern, backwards on a ship

explanation.surface: Something is blown backwards towards the west.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to drift lightly through the air, as a scent carried on the breeze.

clue.text: Given a talent that shows from one's earliest days

indicators.note: that shows indicates the answer can be seen inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A talent that has shown itself since childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'giveN A TALent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal relates to birth, so a natal gift dates from the very start of life.

clue.text: Measure of insulation applied to a classic garment

parts.note: the tog is a unit of thermal resistance used to rate duvets

explanation.surface: An insulation rating is given to an ancient Roman robe.
explanation.walkthrough: TOG is the British unit for how warm a duvet or quilt is.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the robe of ancient Rome, a garment of the classical world.

clue.text: The upper crust taking workers' side

parts.note: worker bees, so workers can mean bees
a wing is a side of a building or of a team

explanation.surface: The aristocracy sides with the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The upper crust' suggests the elite, but it is the filmy crust that forms on top of old port.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswing is the flaky film of tartar that forms on long-kept port wine.

clue.text: Caribbean association makes configuration of power

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for West Indies in the Caribbean
a ring is a group or association of people, as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A Caribbean trade body shapes the balance of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring is the arrangement of electrical cables that carry current through a building.

clue.text: Repeater is to gain applause, keeping time to the second

parts.note: to win is to gain

indicators.note: keeping means holding other letters within

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of applause

indicators.note: to means the letter for time is attached to the letter for second

explanation.surface: A repeat performer wins applause while keeping time to the second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' holds ST inside CHEER, giving CHESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester is a famous lever-action repeating rifle, firing shots in succession.

clue.text: Guerrilla officer's love' for musician

parts.note: the Contras were Nicaraguan guerrillas
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A rebel officer's sweetheart is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is a singer with the lowest female voice, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Shopkeepers concerned with announcement of outfitters

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: announcement says the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: tailors make clothes, outfitting people

explanation.surface: Shop owners care about how outfitters are advertised.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers sell goods to the public from shops.

clue.text: Run ahead of what comes out of volcano in eruption

indicators.note: ahead of places the letter for run in front

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ash is thrown out by a volcano

explanation.surface: People flee from a volcano spewing ash in eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' seems volcanic, but here it is a skin outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin, a medical eruption.

clue.text: In marsh, see river plant

indicators.note: In tells us the letter for river goes inside the word for marsh

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: A visitor to the marshes is shown a riverside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferns are flowerless plants with feathery fronds, common in damp places.

clue.text: One of over a hundred pets, so sweet?

definitions.text: One of over a hundred pets
definitions.meaning: a Dalmatian, one of the hundred and one in the story
a sweet is a dessert, here a suet pudding dotted with currants

explanation.surface: A pet among many is described as sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The hundred-plus pets are the 101 Dalmatians; the sweet is a British suet pudding with currants.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a dog with spots; the pudding is a currant-studded steamed suet dessert.

clue.text: Dim ex-schoolboy's given parish

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, with the possessive S
a cure is a parish or charge in the care of a priest

explanation.surface: A dull former pupil is given a parish to run.
explanation.walkthrough: CURE as a parish comes from a priest's cure of souls.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means dim or faintly visible, not clearly seen.

clue.text: Formality is big part of Murphy's make-up

definitions.meaning: the main nutrient in a potato, a murphy being slang for one

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy is mostly stiffness.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is Irish slang for a potato, which is largely starch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are called starch; potatoes are rich in the carbohydrate of that name.

clue.text: Expedition found. Roman coin among the debris

indicators.note: among puts the coin inside the rearranged letters
debris suggests wreckage, so the letters of the word before it are broken up

parts.note: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: An archaeological expedition finds a Roman coin in the rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a trip but means speed; 'found' is a link, and the period is surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in the sense of promptness or dispatch means speed.

clue.text: Rise to join in hymn, having found something once for collection?

indicators.note: to join in means the word for rise is set inside

parts.note: to hymn is to sing praise
a hill is a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: Churchgoers stand to sing a hymn and then find money for the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, once suitable for the church collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A shilling was an old British coin, the sort once dropped in a church collection plate.

clue.text: One doctor having look round prison

indicators.note: round says the word for look goes around the other letters

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
one is the Roman numeral I
MB is the medical degree Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor looks round a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is slang for prison, or any state of confinement.

clue.text: Material is short for work

indicators.note: is short means the fabric's word loses its final letter

parts.note: toile is a fine linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric is in short supply for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour hard, a synonym of work.

clue.text: This is the way to treat drunkard

parts.note: so means in this way, thus
to use someone is to treat them in a certain way

explanation.surface: A recipe for dealing with a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A souse is slang for a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Chap's empty complaint

indicators.note: the possessive here stands for has, so the man holds the other letter

parts.note: a chap is a man
empty means nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man's complaint has no substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble or complaint.

clue.text: Less polluted area, but one unsuited for preserving salmon?

definitions.meaning: a district where smoke emission is banned
a place where curing fish with smoke would be forbidden

explanation.surface: Clean-air zones are bad news for smokehouses.
explanation.walkthrough: Smokeless zones are UK areas where burning smoky fuel is banned; the joke is that you could not smoke fish there.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean-air district bans smoke-producing fuel; humorously, nobody could smoke fish there.
